sec: Antibodies, Triad of Manifestations & Clinical Presentation

items.q: Match the autoantibody to its percentage positivity on page 911 — 1) Thyroid Stimulating Hormone-Receptor Ab (TRAb) 2) Thyroglobulin Ab 3) TPO Ab … A) +ve 80 - 95% (most important in Graves) B) +ve 50 - 70% (most important in Hashimoto) C) +ve 50 - 80%
items.exp: TRAb is positive in 80-95% (most important in Graves); Thyroglobulin Ab in 50-70% (most important in Hashimoto); TPO Ab in 50-80%. (Book p911)

items.q: TSH-Receptor antibodies stimulate T-cells, fibroblasts, and GAG synthesis to produce which triad of unique clinical findings in Graves' disease?
opts: Thyroid ophthalmopathy, Thyroid dermopathy (pretibial myxedema), and Thyroid acropachy
Periorbital edema, macroglossia, and hoarse voice
Carpal tunnel syndrome, delayed reflexes, and bradycardia
Sensorineural hearing loss, goiter, and periodic paralysis
items.exp: TRAb stimulates T-cells, fibroblasts, and GAGs, leading to the unique triad of Graves: Thyroid ophthalmopathy, Thyroid Dermopathy (Pretibial myxedema), and Thyroid Acropachy. (Book p911)

items.q: Match the unique physical findings of Graves' disease shown in the photographs — 1) Eye pathology 2) Lower extremity dermopathy 3) Digits … A) Severe proptosis, eyelid retraction, and exophthalmos B) Pretibial myxedema (thick nodular infiltrative dermopathy) C) Acropachy
items.exp: The photographs illustrate proptosis/eyelid retraction/exophthalmos, acropachy, and thick nodular infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema). (Book p911)

items.q: Assess common symptoms of thyrotoxicosis: I Restlessness, irritability, tremulousness, nervousness, and tachycardia. II Sweating, diarrhea, polyuria, warm moist skin, and oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: All listed features are documented under Common Features of thyrotoxicosis on page 911. (Book p911)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the common features of thyrotoxicosis on page 911?
opts: Severe constipation and dry cold coarse skin
Tachycardia, sweating, and warm moist skin
items.exp: Constipation and dry cold skin are classic hypothyroid features; thyrotoxicosis features diarrhea, warm moist skin, tachycardia, and sweating. (Book p911)

items.q: An 76-year-old man presents with profound lethargy, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss without tremors or hyperactive behavior. TFTs confirm thyrotoxicosis. What clinical entity does this represent?
items.exp: Under In Elder Population: 'Apathetic thyrotoxicosis : Fatigue and weight loss'. (Book p911)

items.q: In an elderly patient with elevated T3 and T4 levels, which cardiac manifestation is emphasized on page 911?
opts: Atrial fibrillation and worsening of heart failure
Aortic valve stenosis with low-voltage complexes
items.exp: Under Other Features: 'Atrial fibrillation ↑ T3 T4 (mainly elderly)' and 'Worsening of heart failure'. (Book p911)

items.q: A 32-year-old male with severe thyrotoxicosis has proximal muscle weakness of the hips and shoulders. Muscle examination demonstrates NO fasciculations. What is the clinical significance of absent fasciculations per page 911?
opts: Confirms thyrotoxic proximal myopathy from protein catabolism; presence of fasciculations would indicate anterior horn cell disease
Rules out myopathy and indicates psychogenic conversion weakness
Establishes primary polymyositis requiring muscle biopsy
items.exp: Under Severe Thyrotoxicosis: 'Proximal myopathy: No fasciculations (If fasciculations +ve -> Anterior horn cell disease)'. (Book p911)

items.q: In severe thyrotoxicosis: I Protein catabolism leads to bone pain, fractures, and hypercalcemia with hypercalciuria (stones). II Thyrotoxicosis-associated periodic paralysis presents like hypokalemic paralysis.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Severe thyrotoxicosis causes protein catabolism -> proximal myopathy, bone pain/fractures, hypercalcemia -> hypercalciuria -> stones; periodic paralysis presents like hypokalemia paralysis. (Book p911)

items.q: Match the clinical triad to the diagnosis in the page 911 contrast note — 1) Weight loss + good appetite 2) Weight gain + loss of appetite … A) Graves' disease B) Hypothyroidism
items.exp: Page 911 notes: 'Wt loss + good appetite -> Graves disease' and 'Wt gain + loss of appetite -> Hypothyroid'. (Book p911)

items.q: Thyrotoxicosis-associated periodic paralysis presents with acute episodic flaccid quadriparesis resembling ___ paralysis.
items.exp: Under Thyrotoxicosis Associated Periodic paralysis: 'Presents like hypokalemia paralysis'. (Book p911)

items.q: Which guidelines for Graves' disease symptoms are cited at the base of page 911?
items.exp: At the bottom of page 911: 'Endocrine Society of India - Guidelines for Graves : Above mentioned symptoms'. (Book p911)
